heading: Part 1: Branding Permission
body:
This part will demonstrate how to edit which roles have the permission associated with managing a workspace's branding color and logo.
Note: only user's whose role has this permission enabled will be able to perform the following actions.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App , navigate to " Settings " -> click " Roles & Permissions ".
- Select a role to edit -> enable the " Workspace Management " manage checkbox.
- Click " Save " in the bottom right corner to apply any changes made.
- Only users assigned to a role with this permission enabled will be able to manage the workspace color and logo.

heading: Part 2: Manage Branding

  - Note : in the example screenshots, the workspace color is pink .

- A workspace " Logo " can be updated by clicking or dragging a file to the upload area.

  - Note : maximum file size is 5MB .

heading: Part 1: Accessing Amplify
body:
After initial sign up, accounts owners/admins will be able to access Amplify from the SalesRabbit Web App. Amplify is a powerful that allows users to set up a dashboard to report number regarding metrics, set up competitions, and other reporting/gamification capabilities.
Note: some features in Amplify may be limited, depending on your SalesRabbit Plan type.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App, navigate to " Amplify " in the upper left corner.

- A new tab will open, taking users to their Amplify account.

heading: Part 2: Analytics Setup Checklist
body:
Now that you have access to your Amplify account, here are some high priority items to complete to make your Amplify account functional for your organization.

- Assign the SalesRabbit Statuses to Amplify Stages .
  - SalesRabbit Lead Statuses can be assigned to an Amplify Stage from the SalesRabbit Web App . Amplify Stage changes are then reported on the " Pipeline Stages " Dashboard within Amplify.

- Define/Create Metrics to track lead status changes.
  - Metrics are the heart of everything in Amplify. Metric are used to track data on dashboard(s), in competitions, and achievements.

- Manage Dashboard Widgets.
  - Learn to manage the widgets and metrics reporting on the default " Company Admin Dashboard ". Users are able to change what is reporting on any existing board, additionally able to create new boards.

- Manage Amplify User Permissions.
  - Update a Amplify user's permissions to allow specific users access to view data, manage competitions, achievements, and rewards.
  - Owners/Admins are able to adjust user permissions by click on " Manage " in the bottom left corner -> navigating to " Users ".

heading: Part 2: Create a Webhook
body:
This part will cover how to create/manage a webhook for your workspace.

- From the Web App , navigate to " Integrations " -> select " Webhooks ".
- Click the " Create Webhook " button in the upper right corner to create a new webhook.

- From the right pop-out, enter the following information:
  - Title : provide a title for the webhook in this field.
  - URL : paste the URL for the webhook in this field.
  - Event Type : choose the event type (trigger) to send information. Available triggers include:
    - Form Triggers :
      - Form Submitted: event triggers every time a specific form /multiple selected forms are submitted.

    - Lead Triggers :
      - Lead Created: triggers when a lead is created with a specific lead status.
      - Lead Updated: triggers when a lead marked with a specific status is updated (incl. lead status change, name/email/phone/address/etc. updates).
      - Any time a lead with a specific status is updated (incl. lead status change, name/email/phone/address/etc. updates)
      - Lead Deleted: triggers when a lead with a specific lead status is deleted.
      - Lead Status Updated: triggers when a lead is updated to a specific status.
      - Lead Owner Modified: triggers when a specific lead status has the assignee/owner updated.
      - Event Sub-Type : this dropdown will appear for webhooks based on a lead trigger. use the dropdown field to select the lead status(es) acting as the trigger for the webhook.

    - Area Triggers :
      - Area Created: triggers when a new area is created.
      - Area Updated: triggers when an area is updated (Area Name Change, Team/Assignee Updates, Color Updates).
      - Area Deleted: triggers when a new area is deleted.

- Click the " Create " button to save your webhook.

- The new webhook will display under the list of "Active" webhooks.
- Select the three dot icon to the right to " Edit ", " Deactivate ", or " Delete " an active webhook at any time.
  - Note : Deactivated webhooks will live under the "Deactivated" list on the same page and can be " Activated " .

heading: Part 2: Create a Webhook
body:
Webhook FAQs

- What is the difference between a Webhook and an API?
  - Webhook : a mechanism that allows one system to send real-time data to another system automatically when a specific event occurs. It "pushes" information to a designated URL without requiring the receiving system to check for the updates.
  - API (Application Programming Interface) : a set of rules and protocols that allows one system to request data from another system. It requires systems to "pull" information by making calls to retrieve data. API requires "polling" AKA the API is constantly looking for updates at whatever the defined time is (searches for updates every 10min).
  - Key difference: webhooks push data automatically when events happen, while APIs require you to actively request data.

heading: Part 2: Create a Webhook
body:
API requires "polling" AKA the API is constantly looking for updates at whatever the defined time is (searches for updates every 10min).
  - Key difference: webhooks push data automatically when events happen, while APIs require you to actively request data. Think of webhooks as notifications that come to you, and APIs as you calling to ask for information.

- Where can I send data through webhooks?
  - Automation Platforms (Zapier, Make.com/Integromat, Tray.io): these are "middlemen" that catch the data an dpass it to 5,000+ other apps without writing code.
  - CRMs & ERPs (HubSpot, Salesforce, Job Nimbus, Rooflink): the data goes here to update a lead's status, create an invoice, or start a project.
  - Communication Tools (Slack, Microsoft Teams, Twilio): the data triggers a notification so a manager knows a deal was just closed.
  - Custom Servers (AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions): advanced customers send data to their own private databases or custom-built apps.

- Note : almost every modern business tool provides a unique URL in its settings specifically designed to "catch" data sent from webhooks .

heading: What happens if I decide to cancel before my renewal date?
body: - SalesRabbit accounts will remain active for the full contract length. However, if you'd like to cancel your SalesRabbit subscription, you can reach out to the SalesRabbit Support Team or Customer Account Manager Team to make sure it won't renew at the end of your current term. You may also refer to your contract for more information on our refund policy.

heading: Am I charged for deactivated users?
body: - Workspaces are not charged for the number of deactivated users. Workspaces are billed by the number of active user licenses , or the number of active users if greater than the number of active licen ses.
text:
Getting Started > SR+ Billing FAQ :: Am I charged for deactivated users?

- Workspaces are not charged for the number of deactivated users. Workspaces are billed by the number of active user licenses , or the number of active users if greater than the number of active licen ses.
title: SR+ Billing FAQ

heading: How do I know how many user licenses I'm being billed for?
body:
- Upon sign up, the SalesRabbit Account Executive will help you determine a minimum number of user licenses for the workspace. Workspace Owners/Admins are then responsible to manage the number of users on the account based on how many active licenses you need. SalesRabbit bills for " active" user licenses at or above your user minimum.
  - For example :
    - If your workspace has 20 active users and there are still 20 active users when your next billing cycle begins, you will again be billed for the 20 users.
    - If three users are deactivated in the middle of a billing cycle and now have 17 active users, you may add or reactivate up to 3 users at no additional cost.
    - If adding (or reactivating) users beyond the number of available user licenses you started the billing cycle with, we will generate a new invoice and bill for the additional licenses.

heading: Does SalesRabbit prorate user license costs?
body:
- Yes. If you add or activate users beyond the “high-water mark” during a billing cycle, we will bill a prorated cost for those users based on the amount of time remaining in the billing cycle.
- We do not prorate costs for users that are deactivated in the middle of a billing cycle, however, this does free up an active user license(s) allowing you to reactivate/add new users at no additional cost.

heading: Can I add "add-on" products to my account (e.g. DataGrid AI) and only have some licenses be billed for them?

heading: When will I be billed?
body:
- Not every account will be the same. The date you are billed will be determined by the day your service with SalesRabbit began and will follow your subscription plan (monthly, quarterly, or annual). Here's an explanation on how billing cycles work depending on your subscription plan:
- Annual Billing : when adding users, they're billed for the remainder of your annual term.
  - Example: if you add users in month 6 of a 12-month term, you'll be billed for the remaining 6-months.
  - Next Renewal: at the start of the next annual term, you'll be billed for all active users on the account for the full 12-month term.

- Quarterly Billing : you're billed for each quarter upfront.

- Annual Billing : when adding users, they're billed for the remainder of your annual term.

  - Next Renewal: at the start of the next annual term, you'll be billed for all active users on the account for the full 12-month term.

heading: Part 1: Appointments on Leads Page
body:
This part will cover the out-of-the-box appointment setting function for leads on the Web App "Leads" page.

- Appointments can be set on leads from the " Leads " page and the " Map " page on the Web App.
- From the " Leads " page, click the " Add Lead " button or select an existing lead.

- Once in the " Lead Detail " page, use the " Appointment " field to select a day & time for the appointment.
- After selecting a day & time, don't forget to click " Save " in the bottom right corner.

- Leads with a scheduled appointment day & time will be visible from the " Leads " page under the " Appointment " columns.

- Tip : filter for leads with an appointment scheduled within a specific date range with the " Appointment Filter " on the "Leads" page .

body:

- Historical Data: Access to past location data for performance analysis and route optimization.

body:

This part will demonstrate to how send a simple message to another user.

- Once in " Messages ", users will see a inbox of message threads of previous conversations.
- To send a new message to another user, click the " + " icon in the upper right corner or select the existing thread conversation with that user.

- Select the user you'd like to send a message to -> click " Done ".
  - Note : a user will only be able to message other users on their assigned team or associated sub-team .

- Use the " Write a Message " text box to draft and send a message to that specific user.
- Additionally, add attachments and gifs with the icons to the left of the text box.

heading: Important Limitations
body:
- SalesForce API rate limits apply and should be monitored
  - Organizations should monitor API usage to avoid hitting daily limits.

- Custom object syncing requires additional configuration and may need technical support.
- Large file attachments (>2GB) cannot be synced due to SalesForce file size limitations.
  - Note : Larger file attachments via API can timeout, best practice would be to keep them closer to 25MB.

- Some SalesForce validation rules may prevent records from syncing - these need to be reviewed during setup.
- Real-time sync depends on webhook availability (fallback polling occurs every 5 minutes).
- Multi-currency features require additional configuration.
- The integration architecture support bidirectional sync (push/pull/both), but the current production implementation is PUSH-ONLY (SalesRabbit -> SalesForce) with ID writeback for record linking. Future releases may enable pull functionality for field values and statuses.

heading: Article Overview
body:
The SalesRabbit+ API is a powerful integration tool that allows customers to programmatically access and interact with their SalesRabbit Data. It provides a standardized way to connect SalesRabbit with other business systems, enabling seamless data flow between platforms and automating critical sales workflows.
Through RESTful endpoints, the API gives customers the ability to retrieve lead information, update sales data, manage team activities, and synchronize records in real-time with their existing CRM, marketing automation, or business intelligence tools.
text:
Integrations > Public API+ :: Article Overview

The SalesRabbit+ API is a powerful integration tool that allows customers to programmatically access and interact with their SalesRabbit Data. It provides a standardized way to connect SalesRabbit with other business systems, enabling seamless data flow between platforms and automating critical sales workflows.
Through RESTful endpoints, the API gives customers the ability to retrieve lead information, update sales data, manage team activities, and synchronize records in real-time with their existing CRM, marketing automation, or business intelligence tools.
title: Public API+

heading: Why It's Important to Customers
body:
Fro enterprise customers and growing organizations, the Public API is essential infrastructure that transforms SalesRabbit from a standalone tool into the central hub of their sales technology ecosystem.

- Eliminates Manual Data Entry: automatically sync lead and sales data between SalesRabbit and other systems, reducing errors and saving countless hours of administrative work.

heading: Part 1: Rewards Permission
body:
In order to manage an account's reward shop, a user must have the Rewards Permission enabled for their Amplify user. This part will walk through how to check if a user has the Rewards permission enabled for their Amplify user.

- Log in to Amplify on the web -> select the " Manage " in the bottom left corner -> click " Users ".

- Select the desired user -> click " Admin Access ".

- Ensure that the user either has " Company Access " or, specifically, the " Reward " permission enabled.
- Don't forget to click " Save Changes " before navigating away!

heading: Part 2: Reward Shop Management
body:
This part will demonstrate how to manage the items available in your Amplify Reward Shop. Items in the shop are also visible from the Amplify mobile app.

- Log in to Amplify on the web -> select the " Rewards " tab from the left menu.
- There are many sections within the rewards tab.

- Items listed in the " Reward Shop " are items that users can purchase with the coins they have earned.
- To add a new reward to your shop, select " + New Reward " in the upper right corner..

- When creating a reward, users will need to provide a " Title ", a " Description ", set the numbers of " Coins " you'd like the reward to be worth in the shop, and edit additional reward settings such as limiting the quantity, auto-approval, limit period, purchase limit...
  - Tip : best practice is to track coins based on a 10:1 ratio (an item that costs my company $100 should be worth 1,000 coins in the shop).

- After setting up your new reward, click " Add " at the bottom.

- Existing rewards can be edited/disabled by selecting the three dot icon on the reward itself.
  - Tip : any disabled rewards are accessible by selecting the " Disabled " button on the Reward Shop.

- If a user purchases an item with their coins, it will appear as a request under " Requests & Transactions ".
- Admins must approve/decline all reward purchases.

- Potential Transaction Statuses:
  - Completed
  - Pending
  - Declines: for rewards requests where the admin chose to deny the purchase for whatever reason.
  - Cancelled: for rewards requests where the user withdrew the purchase before it could be approved.
  - Refunded: for rewards requests that were initially approved, but needed to be retroactively withdrawn for whatever reason.
  - Aborted: a fairly raree status taht indicates the transaction in question failed to complete.

heading: Part 3: Coins Setup
body:
Admins can automate how their users earn coins under the "Coins Setup" tab.

- Under the " Coins Setup " tab, admins are able to establish how reps can earn coins through earning Achievements or marking specific lead statuses.

- Whether assigning coin values to Achievements or Activities (marking specific lead statuses), select the category -> locate the Achievement/Lead Status -> enter the value of coins a user should automatically earn upon earning the Achievement/marking the lead status.
- Click " Save Changes " once complete.

- Users will now be able to earn coins when they earn an Achievement or mark a lead with a designated lead status!

heading: Part 4: Earnings
body:
This part will cover the "Earnings" tab in the Rewards section. This page provides a quick summary of users' activity for a designated period, displaying how many coins have gone in and out of their account, how many coins are being hel din reserve for prize purchases or battle bets, and a current balance.
Note: if you do not have admin access, you will only see your own name here.

- Under " Earnings " admins will find a list of each Amplify user, along with how many coins they have earned.
- Coins listed on the earnings page are coins that a user can spend on items in the reward shop.
- After setting a date range, admins will be able to view:
  - How many coins that user has earned within that period.
  - How many coins the user has spent within that period.
  - How many coins the user has on reserve, or towards ongoing battles/purchases.
  - Each user's overall spending balance.

heading: Part 5: Coins Budget
body:
This part will cover how to manage your coins budget. Amplify allows account admins to assign budgets for admins, enabling a controlled spending on competitions and endorsements.

- Under " Coins Budget ", admins will find a list of other admins or users who have the Rewards permission enabled.
- Admins are able to use the coins from their budget to offer coins as a reward in competitions and do spot endorsements.
  - Note : In order to offer coins as a reward in competitions, you must have coins in your budget!

- After setting a date range, admins will be able to view:
  - How many budgeted coins that user has received within that period.
  - How many budget coins the user has used within that period.
  - How many budget coins the user has leftover/received from outside of the period.
  - Each user's overall budget coin balance.

- Budget admins can request additional budgets, which account admins can approve or decline.
- Admins can choose to use their budget or own coins for endorsements, with mandatory budget use for competition prizes.
- Account admins have the authority to self-allocate budgets and monitor individual transactions, ensuring expenditures align with company needs.

heading: Part 1: Create a Board for Mobile App Widgets
body:
Learn how to create a new board for the Amplify mobile app. A board presents a collection of statistics in the mobile app. In order to view mobile app widgets on your mobile device, those widgets must live on a board. Boards can be configured by title, team access, access level, and set a default period.

- From the web version of Amplify, navigate to the " Dashboard " -> click " Manage Boards ".

- This page will display all available boards in your company.
- To add an app board, navigate to " App Boards " in the upper left.
  - Note: By default, all accounts will have two boards: "Lead Status Activities" and "Lead Stage Activities". Default widgets will exist on those boards. New widgets can be created and assigned to either board.

- Select " + Add Board " to create a new mobile app board.

- Create a new board:
  - Title : The title of your board. It will be shown in the mobile application.
  - Team Access : If you want to limit which teams can access the board, choose a subset of teams in this dropdown. If no access limitations are intended, leave it as is.
  - Access Level : Choose what types of access rights are needed to see the board.

heading: Part 2: Create a New Board
body:
When creating a new board, users are able to edit the board's description, restrict which users can view the board, and which filters are available for that board.

- After selecting " + Add New Board ", Users will be presented with several setup options for their new board.
  - General :
    - Title: provide a title for the new board.
    - Description: give a description of the new board.
    - Default Period: set the default period for data to display.
    - Category: assign the board to an existing category.
    - Icon: select an icon to represent this new board.

  - Board Access :
    - Teams/Departments: select which teams/departments are able to view the board.
    - Access level: select which access level a user must have to view the board.

  - Filters :
    - Resource Intensive: when checked, users won't be able to add new widgets to this board.
    - User Filter: allows for users to filter data on the board by user.
    - Team Filter: allows for users to filter data on the board by team.
    - Activity Filter: allows for users to filter data on the board by activity type.
    - Show Current User's Data by Default: choose to display the signed in user's data by default.

- Click " + Add Board " to create your new board.

- After creating your new board, users are able to reassign the board to a different category and reorganize the order the boards are listed within that category.
- Additionally, existing boards can be edited, copied, hidden, and deleted from the Manage Boards page.

- Live boards will be visible from the main Dashboard in Amplify.

body:
After creating a new board, users will then need to create any necessary Metrics and create Widgets for those metrics to report on an existing board!

Pro Tips

- Configure the access of a board if you want to restrict/hide the data from a group of employees because the data is confidential or not relevant for the group.

heading: Part 1: Appointment Permissions
body:
This part will cover the 4 permissions for Advanced Appointment Management. The ability for a user to configure team availability, schedule/accept appointments, and other calendar permissions is dependent on the user's role permissions.

- Navigate to the appointment permissions by selecting " Settings " -> " Roles & Permissions " in the web app -> s elect the role that you'd like to edit the permissions for.
- Scroll through the permissions until you find a section for " Appointments ".
  - There are 4 permissions related to advanced appointment management:
    - Appointment Settings:
      - Allows the team member to configure team availability, appointment distribution, and lead status updates for scheduled appointments.

    - Schedule Appointments:
      - Enables the team member to schedule appointments on behalf of other team members.

    - Accept Appointments:
      - Enables the team member to appear as an option for appointment scheduling.

    - Calendar:
      - Allows the role to view and manage appointments across your entire team from a calendar view on the web app and mobile app.

- Be sure to click " Save " in the bottom right corner to apply any changes.

heading: Part 2: Appointment Settings
body:
This part will cover the general appointment settings that are reflected across your entire Workspace.

- Navigate to appointment settings by selecting " Settings " -> " Appointments " from the web app.
- Availability Settings:
  - Days: determine which days all users on the account can be scheduled for.
  - Start/End Times: allows a user to designate a specific time frame that their users can be scheduled for.
  - Update Lead Status: toggling this on will automatically update the status of the scheduled lead to a designated status. In the example below, that status is set to "Appointment Set".

- Distribution Settings:
  - Rep's Choice: allows the rep the ability to choose who's calendar they'd like to schedule an appointment for.
  - Round Robin: provides the rep with all currently available times, regardless of a specific rep's availability.

- Be sure to click " Save " in the bottom right corner to apply your changes.

heading: Part 3: Adding Your Calendar - Web App
body:
This part will cover how to add a calendar to your SalesRabbit+ user from the Web App. Adding a calendar to each user is an essential step to fully utilize Advanced Appointment Scheduling features. Users will not be able to schedule appointments for others until they've connected their calendar through either the Web App or Mobile App. Note:Users can also connect a calendar on their own device in the mobile app home settings.

- Login to the SalesRabbit+ Web App .
- Click the profile icon in the upper right corner -> select " My Account ".

- Under the " Calendar " section, a logged in user can connect or add a calendar to be used with Advanced Appointment Management.
- To connect a calendar, click " Sync Calendar ".
  - Syncing a calendar will require the user to allows SalesRabbit+ permission to schedule on that calendar.

- Once a calendar has been synced, the connected calendar email will display under the words " Calendar Synced ".

- You've successfully added a calendar and are ready to schedule appointments for others!
- A synced calendar can be disconnected from the account by selecting the trash can icon.

heading: Part 1: Accessing Your Mobile App Profile Settings
body:
Access the mobile app profile settings by selecting the profile icon in the upper right hand corner from the Home Tab. Mobile App Profile settings that can be adjusted include the following:

- Profile
  - Add a user profile photo by selecting an existing photo or taking a photo.

- Lead Appointments
  - Toggling ON " Sync to Default Calendar " will sync set lead appointment date/times to the default calendar on your device.
  - Users can set a reminder before any of their scheduled appointments. Reminders will come through as a push notification.

- Preferences
  - Select " Push Notifications " to manage which notifications you'd like to receive from SalesRabbit+.

  - Available push notifications include assigned appointments, area assignments, and leads ownership assignments. Users are encouraged to enable/disable any of these notifications using the toggles to the right.

- Map
  - Enabling " User Location Path ": will connect user location markers that appear on the SalesHub map with a line.

heading: Part 1: Accessing Your Mobile App Profile Settings
body:
Users are encouraged to enable/disable any of these notifications using the toggles to the right.

- Map
  - Enabling " User Location Path ": will connect user location markers that appear on the SalesHub map with a line. Making it possible to follow the route a user took.
  - Enabling " Display Lead Names ": will display the First and Last name of a lead on the SalesHub Map.
  - Enabling " Proximity Indicator ": will display a small icon in the upper right hand corner of each lead with one of the following indicator icons:
    - Green checkmark : At Location (within ~25m).
    - Yellow checkmark : Near Location (within ~75-100m).
    - Red exclamation point : Not at Location (>100m).
    - Uknown: will appear when the user's location is unavailable.

  - " Turn-by-Turn Navigation ": allows users to select their preferred navigation tool when creating routes .
  - " Distance Units ": allows users to set their preferred distance unit (Imperial vs. Metric).
  - " Language ": allows users to select a language preference.

heading: Article Overview
body:
Imagine a treasure map where an address tells you where to go, and extra notes help you find the treasure faster. URL parameters are like those extra notes. They are tiny pieces of information added to the end of a website link (URL) that help a system understand what you want it to do.
TIP:URL Parameters work hand-in-hand with SalesRabbit Quick Links. Quick Links are only available to Pro Accounts or higher.

title: URL Parameters

heading: Part 1: URL Parameters
body:
- Here is an example of a basic URL: https://example.com
- Here is an example of a URL with Parameters: https://example.com?name=John&age=30
  - The " ? " starts the parameters.
  - Multiple pieces of information are separated by "&".
  - Another example of URL Anatomy with Parameters:

- When using Quick Links in SalesRabbit+, you'll map a parameter, like " name={Name} ", making the value dynamic . That means it changes based on the data from SalesRabbit. So, instead of the value always being 'John" it would pass the name on the lead.
  - When mapped in SalesRabbit, it would appear as " name={Name} " in the URL.

heading: Part 2: Why Use URL Parameters with Quick Links
body:
- Quick Links allow you to send information from SalesRabbit to other Systems, saving you from double entry. If you want to send a customer's name and phone number to another form, adding URL parameters will automatically populate and pass that data for you.
  - For example, when creating a SalesRabbit Quick Link for a Calendly link, if the Calendly link has parameters in the URL, lead information will pre-fill fields on the Calendly booking page.

heading: Part 3: How to Find the Right Parameters
body:
- Check your form: open the form you want to link to and inspect the URL when you fill in a field. Sometimes, the URL will show the parameter (this is the most straightforward path).
- Ask ChatGPT for Help: If you're not sure which parameters your form uses, you can try this prompt within ChatGPT:
  - " I'm using [Your Form's URL] and want to know which URL parameters it accepts. Can you help me find them? "
    - Once you know your parameters, you can then either:
      - Build the URL yourself (you now have the formula, remember: url.com?field=&field-2=)

    - Ask ChatGPT to build the URL for you:
      - " I'd like to include the following parameters:... Please build a URL with the outlined parameters "

- Test It Out: add your URL (with those added parameters!) in the Quick Links creation drawer.
  - You'll know if it's working if the creation drawer presents fields for you to map.

- Note : Other softwares will typically have an article or resource detailing their parameters.
  - Calendly URL Parameters Help Center

heading: Part 4: Testing Your Quick Link
body:
- Copy the link you've made with your parameters.
- Paste it in a new browser tab and press Enter
- If the form displays the parameters, like "{name}" and "{email}", in the proper fields... you did it right!

- If it doesn't work, or the form fields are empty, double-check your parameters or reach out to our support team for assistance.

Pro Tips

- Make sure the parameters match the form's exact names (capitalization matters).
- A Parameter Reference Sheet for fields in SalesRabbit can be found when creating a Quick Link
- Check for extra spaces in the URL (this can throw you of, especially if there is a space at the beginning of the URL).
- Make sure to use "&" to separate multiple parameters

heading: Article Overview
body:
Quick Links function as the bridge between the SalesRabbit platform and other essential software tools used by our clients. They facilitate the seamless transfer of data, ensuring that all relevant customer and sales information is readily accessible across different platforms.
This feature allows for enhanced efficiency in various areas such as customer relationship management, sales tracking, and data analysis. By reducing the need for manual data entry, Quick Links can significantly decrease the chances of errors while improving productivity.
Quick Links can be used for simple things (like opening a link to their Google Business account to show potential customers their rating) to action-oriented items (like scheduling an appointment through Calendly) to passing data into a form (like submitting lead information into a custom form created by the customer).
TIP:This feature is available to Pro accounts or higher.

heading: Part 1: Quick Links Permissions
body:
There are permissions associated with accessing and creating Quick Links.

- To manage the Quick Links permissions, navigate to " Settings " -> " Roles & Permissions " -> select desired role -> find the " Quick Links " permission under the General section.
- Admins can decide if a specific role is able to View and/or Manage Quick Links for their account.
  - View Permission: allows a specific role the ability to view created Quick Links on the Web App.
    - Note: Admins can also manage which users have access to certain Quick Links when creating the Quick Link itself.

  - Manage Permissions: allow a specific role the ability to create/edit new and existing Quick Links access and visibility.

- If making changes to a role's permission, click " Save " to apply your changes.

heading: Part 2: Setup Quick Links on Web App
body:

Adding URL Parameters to a Quick Link will allow lead information to pass over to a form or booking page, preventing unnecessary double data entry.

- From the Web App, navigate to " Settings " -> select " Quick Links ".
- Select the " Create " button to set up a new Quick Link.

- From the right menu:
  - Title : name your new Quick Link.

  - URL : copy and paste your URL into the URL box.
    - Optionally, if setting up a form or booking page link, add and map the URL Parameters so that lead information can pass over onto the form/booking page instantly.
    - Note : click the "Show Reference" button to display a reference sheet for SR parameter fields.

  - Visibility : choose which users/teams to give mobile app access to this quick link.

heading: Part 2: Folder Creation
body:
This section demonstrates how to manage the Sales Materials Folder Tree. Creating designated folders allow users to better organize their Sales Materials.

- From the SalesRabbit Web app , navigate to " SalesHub " -> click " Sales Materials ".
- The folder tree will can be found near the middle of the screen.

- When creating a new folder, provide a folder " Name " -> click the " Create " button.

- Selecting on an existing folder allows users to create a folder within the selected folder using the " + Create Folder " button.
  - Note : users are able to create a folder within an existing folder as well.

- When selecting an existing folder, users are also able to:
  - View previously uploaded materials that were previously assigned to that folder.
  - " Upload " materials to the selected folder.
  - Select the three dot icon to " Rename / Delete " the selected folder.
  - Note : use the " + Create Folder " button to create another folder within the selected folder .

heading: Part 3: Add Sales Materials
body:
In this section, we will go over how to add and remove Sales Material into your account. Materials can be uploaded as either a file/document or a URL can be added as a material.

- Go to hop.salesrabbit.com and log into your account.
- From the left menu, navigate to " SalesHub " -> click " Sales Materials ".
- Clicking the " Upload " button will allow users to add any Sales Materials that your team may need.

- Select the " Sales Material Type " you are uploading:
  - File : upload a file from your desktop to be accessed by users from the mobile app.

- URL : add a URL that can be easily accessible by users from the mobile app.

- Under " Location ", select the folder this sales material will live under.
- Under " File " or "URL", click or drag the file to upload or provide the desired URL.
- Under " File Name " provide a name for the new Sales Material.
  - Note : oftentimes the file name will default to the name of your uploaded file.

- Click " Upload " to save your new file.
- To " Edit " or " Delete " previously uploaded materials, click the three dots on the right hand side of the file and select the desired action.

- Supported Image :
  - JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg)
  - PNG (.png)
  - GIF (.gif), including animated GIFs
  - WebP (.webp), including animated WebP
  - HEIC (.heic)
  - TIFF (.tif, .tiff)

- Supported Documents :
  - PDF (.pdf)

- Supported Video :
  - MP4 (.mp4)
  - MOV (.mov)
  - 3GP (.3pg)

- Supported Audio :
  - AAC (.aac)
  - MP3 (.mp3)
  - MAV (.wav)

heading: Part 2: Managing Teams
body:
This part will cover how to manage your teams by making changes to the structure, name, and users to your teams.

- You'll want to manage your Teams to make sure the structure is best designed for your organization.
- Teams can have multiple tiers and sub-teams.
- As shown below, " Gryffindor " lives under " Hogwarts ".
  - Note : additionally, there are 3 users assigned to the "Gryffindor" team.

- Renaming and Deleting teams can be done under the " Actions " button in the upper right corner.
  - To do so, select the team you'd like to rename/delete.
  - Then, click on the " Actions " drop down menu and select either " Edit " or " Delete ".
    - Edit: allows users to change the team name.
    - Delete: allows users to delete a team.
      - Note: All users must be removed from a team in order to delete. Attempting to delete a team containing assigned users will return an error message.

- TIP: Users can move sub-teams to different team by clicking and dragging on the "sub-team" name underneath the new team.

heading: Part 1: DataGrid AI Permissions
body:
This part explains how to manage a role's DataGrid permissions within SalesRabbit+. Available permissions include DataGrid Areas, DataGrid Buyer Scores, and DataGrid On-Demand.

- From the Web App , navigate to " Settings " -> click " Roles & Permisssions ".
  - DataGrid AI permissions are editable by Role.

- Available DataGrid Permissions :
  - DataGrid Areas : view or manage areas with aggregated buyer scores by state, country, or census blocks and assign them to users to work leads in that specific area.
  - DataGrid AI Buyer Scores : view the buyer propensity scores in DataGrid Areas and DataGrid pins.
  - DataGrid On-Demand : view DataGrid AI pins on homes within a 300m radius from the user's physical location (no need to assign areas in order to see DataGrid pins).

- If making changes to a role's permissions, click " Save " in the bottom right corner.

heading: Part 2: Populating DataGrid Pins on the Mobile App
body:
In this part, we cover how to populate DataGrid pins in the SalesRabbit+ mobile app.
Note: DataGrid pins are only accessible from the mobile app and not the web app.

- There are two ways to populate DataGrid pins in the mobile app.
  - If a user's role has the "DataGrid On-Demand" permission turned on, then DataGrid pins will appear within 300m of that user's current physical location.
  - Users will also view/access DataGrid pins on homes inside of areas the user is assigned to.

- To draw and assign an area from the mobile app, select the " Lasso Tool " in the SalesHub.

- From there, circle around a neighborhood/group of homes you'd like to turn into an area.
- Once the shape has been completed, options to add a title, select a team, user, and color will appear.

- Select the desired user for the area. That user will then be able to view/access DataGrid pins on homes inside of the assigned area.
  - Tip: If a user is not seeing DataGrid pins on home in their assigned areas, zoom in on the map a bit closer to the street!

- Note : DataGrid Pins also appear on homes within 300m of a user's location if the user's role has the "DataGrid On-Demand" permission enabled .

heading: Part 3: Convert a DataGrid Pin into a Lead
body:
In this part, we cover how to convert a DataGrid Pin into a Lead.

- Convert a DataGrid Pin into a lead by first selecting a pin on the map.
- The available demographic information for that pin will be visible.
  - Click on any DataGrid pin to view the Home and Home Owner data for that property.
    - Home Data that displays:
      - Year Built
      - Home Price
      - Home Size
      - Residency (How long in home)
      - Occupants
      - Credit Range

    - Home Owner Data that displays:
      - First and Last Name
      - Age
      - Preferred Language
      - Owner/Renter Status
      - Marital Status
      - Combined total Income
      - Phone Number (If Available)

  - Once ready to convert a pin into a Lead, select the " Lead Status Icon " that best represents the interaction with the Prospect.

- Now that you have converted a lead, the name and information from the pin is automatically saved on the lead. Users can add notes from the new pop-up, or click the " Details " button in the top right hand corner to edit the lead info even further.

heading: Part 5: DataGrid Filters
body:
In this part, we cover how to filter your DataGrid AI pins on the mobile app. Filters help users focus on high priority DataGrid pins or that meet a specified criteria that you set.

- In the top left hand corner of the SalesHub Map on the mobile app, select the " Filters " Icon.

- Then click the dropdown arrow next to " DataGrid " filter.

- Scroll through the desired datapoint(s) that you would like to filter by, and set the parameters by clicking " Apply " when finished. This action will remove DataGrid Pins that do not match the standards applied.
- Tip : set the " Occupancy " filter to " Homeowner " which removes DataGrid Pins with renters from the map .

- If you wish to reset filters to the default view, click the " Reset All " button underneath the DataGrid AI filter toggle switch. Pro Tips

- The Occupancy filter is the most popular, as it will allow you to remove pins that have renters.
- Consider data points that will be useful for your industry. Here are some popular examples:
  - Solar
    - Credit Score
    - Length of residence

  - Roofing & Home Improvement
    - Year Home built

- It is still a good idea to knock on every door.

heading: Part 2: Creating a Competition
body:
This part will demonstrate how to create a basic competition from the Amplify Web App.

- To access Amplify, select the " Amplify " option in the left menu from the SalesRabbit Web App.

- A new tab will open in the browser.
- Once in Amplify, navigate to " Competitions " in the left menu -> click the " + Create New " button to create a new competition for your team(s).

- When creating a new competition, you'll first be present with a menu of different types of competitions. Select which type of competition you'd like to host:
  - Standard:
  - Multi-Round:
  - Prize Ladder:
  - Lottery:
  - Bracket:
  - Lucky:
  - Gift Swap:
  - King of the Hill:

- After selecting the type of competition -> click on it and select " Create "X" Competition ".

- When creating a new competition, users will need to do the following:
  - Step 1 : Who is Competing
    - Select which/if users will be competing individually, in Teams, or create custom teams.

  - Step 2 : What (metric) would you like to compete on?
    - Select which metric(s) will be tracked during the competition.

  - Step 3 : When is it?
    - Set the Starting and Ending Date/Time for the competition.

  - Step 4 : Would you like to set goals? (optional)
    - Set a specific goal for each user/team to reach during the competition.

  - Step 5 : Choose your prizes and winners.
    - Create prizes for the competition.
    - Prizes can either be a custom item or coins.
    - Note : if offering coins as a reward for competitions, users will first need coins in their budget to offer them.

  - Step 6 : Review your advanced options.
    - Advanced options include deciding privacy settings, when a winner is declared, and what happens if a tie occurs.

  - Don't forget to give your competition a Title and Description!
  - Click either " Save as Draft " or " Save and Publish " to save your changes!

- To edit an existing/drafted competition, navigate to the " Competitions " tab -> select the three dots icon -> click " Edit ".

  - Click either " Save as Draft " or " Save and Publish " to save your changes!

body:
In this article, we will cover how to setup and configure your Achievements. Achievements offer a dynamic way to motivate your sales team to exceed their targets. They mark important milestones, like achieving a sales budget, breaking a sales record, or closing a significant number of sales in a day. With Amplify, you can create customized achievements that align with your organization's goals. These achievements encompass on-screen announcements, unique soundtracks, badges, and experience points (XP), enhancing team engagement and motivation.
Note: Achievements are available to Pro/Enterprise accounts. Adjustments to achievements can only be made by an Admin or Owner role within your SalesRabbit/Amplify Account.

heading: Part 1: Achievement Permission
body:
In order to manage an account's achievements, a user must have the Achievement Permission enabled for their Amplify user. This part will walk through how to check if a user has the achievement permission enabled for their Amplify user.

- Log in to Amplify on the web -> select the " Manage " in the bottom left corner -> click " Users ".

- Select the desired user -> click " Admin Access ".

- Ensure that the user either has " Company Access " or, specifically, the " Achievement " permission enabled.
- Don't forget to click " Save Changes " before navigating away!

  - Unlock History : who has earned the achievement most recently

- Editing an existing achievement:
  - Metric : select the metric you'd like this specific achievement to be tracked with.
  - Unlock Requirements : allows you to choose what number a user has to earn in order to unlock the achievement.

heading: Part 2: Create an Achievement
body:
In this section, we will show you how to create a new achievement.

- From a desktop, select " Achievements " in the left menu bar -> " Manage Achievements ".
  - Tip : you can also create a new achievement under "Manage" -> "Achievements".

- The Manage Achievements page allows you to edit, copy, disable, or delete an existing achievement. You can also create a brand new achievement from scratch.

- Selecting " + Create New " will pull up an achievement creation page:
  - In the upper left corner, you'll decide if this achievement will be:
    - Goal : achievement earned by surpassing a fixed value, target progression, or a previous period. Once you exceed the threshold, the achievement is unlocked.
      - Example: 10 sales in a single day.

    - High-Score : achievement earned by surpassing the highest sales value, which then becomes the new benchmark for others to beat. The high-score value moves as salespeople outperform each other.
      - Example: highest sales value in a month.

    - Top Performer : achievements awarded based on the best sales performance within a specified time frame.

- Long Press : users can create a new lead by performing a long press on the home/address you're creating a lead for.

body:
Accounts with the DataGrid AI add-on will have the option to create leads using DataGrid Pins. DataGrid pins are accessible on homes inside of that user's assigned areas.
Note: A user whose role has access to the DataGrid On-Demandpermission will also see DataGrid Pins on homes within 300m of the user's current physical location.

A user can easily convert these name tiles into a lead by simply selecting the appropriate lead status on the correct name tile.

- Leads created from DataGrid pins will automatically save the demographic information from the DataGrid pin.
  - To re-access that new lead's demographic information, select the lead on the map and toggle to " DataGrid AI ".

heading: Part 4: Managing Leads Offline
body:
This part will explain offline lead syncing.

- Sometimes service can be spotty when you're out canvassing. If a rep loses service or goes offline for any reason, they will see an " Offline " indicator at the top of the SalesHub Map.

- Leads can still be created when a user is offline.
- As a user creates leads offline, the banner at the top of the SalesHub Map will update with how many leads will need to be synced.

- Once the user's device has a good connection, the banner will begin to sync.
- Once all the leads have been synced, the banner will turn your brand color and you'll be notified that syncing is complete.

Pro Tips

- If your account has DataGrid AI , SalesRabbit recommends creating leads with DataGrid pins so you have access to the most information possible.
- The SalesHub " Street View " can also be used to create/edit lead details.

- From the SalesRabbit+ WebApp , navigate to the " Users " tab in the left menu.

  - View a list of Active or Deactivated users.
  - Add/Manage workspace users.

- Selecting a user will pull up that user's detail page. Users with the appropriate permissions (typically admins), are be able to update:

  - A user's phone number.
  - Add an External ID.
  - The user's color.

- Be sure to click " Save " to apply any changes made to the user.

- Additionally, admins are able to view a user's " Activity ", a historical log of changes made to that user's information.

heading: Part 3: Deactivate a User
body:
This part will cover how to deactivate a user. Deactivating a user means that user will no longer be able to access SalesRabbit unless reactivated. All data assigned to this user (areas, assignments, leads, etc.) will be reassigned to another user. Deactivating a user also reduces the number of seats/user licenses are being occupied occupied.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App, navigate to the " Users " tab in the left menu.
- To quickly deactivate a user, select on the three dots to the right of the desired user -> click " Deactivate ".

- Alternatively, click " View Details " (or select the user itself) to navigate to that user's detail page -> click the " Actions " button in the upper right hand corner -> select the " Deactivate " option.

- When deactivating a user, you'll be prompted to assign that user's data to another user. Assign the data -> click " Deactivate ".

- Deactivated users are visible from the " Users " page under the " Deactivated " list.
- Deactivated users can be reactivated at any time by those with the proper permissions.

body:

    - Lead : will create a lead in SalesForce.

    - Custom Objects : when enabled, opens up the SalesForce Custom Objects table. This table includes drop-downs that will list all custom objects from the authenticated SalesForce account. Note : up to 3 custom objects can be selected.

  - Select the SalesRabbit user that should be the "default" user for creating records in SalesForce.
    - The integration will first try to assign the record to the SalesRabbit Lead Owner based on their External ID in SalesRabbit. If the External ID is blank or doesn't include a valid SalesForce User ID, it will fallback to using that user's email.

heading: Article Overview
body:
This guide provides step-by-step instructions for setting up a lottery competition in Amplify. Lottery competitions add an element of chance, where anyone can win a prize regardless of performance. Top contributors earn more tickets, increasing their odds, but every seller has a shot with just one ticket. It's a fun way to reward participation and keep the team engaged!
TIP:users must be an Amplify admin/owner or have the competition permission enabled in order to perform the following functions.

heading: Part 1: Lottery Competition
body:
This part will demonstrate how to set up a lottery competition within Amplify.

- From the Amplify Web App, navigate to " Competitions " -> select " + Create New ".

- Select " Lottery " -> click " Create Lottery Competition ".

- Complete the following items to set up your competitions:
  - Title : Give this competition a name.

  - Description : Provide a description/objective of the competition.

  - Theme : select the theme for reps to track their progress and view results.

  - Step 1 : Who is Competing?
    - Select which user(s) will be competing in this competition.

  - Step 2 : What would you like to compete on?
    - Select the metric(s) that is going to be tracked and count toward the competition.

  - Step 3 : When is it?

  - Step 4 : Can users obtain multiple prizes?

  - Step 5 : Choose your prizes and winners.

    - Users can choose how may prizes they want to give away in a competition (1, 2, 3, or other).

- Click " Save and Publish ".

- Your new lottery competition will then display under the list of " Active " or " Drafted " competitions.
  - Tip : click the three dots to the right of the listed competition to " Edit ", " End ", or " Delete " a competition.

TIP:The old way of creating leads is still available in the updated version of SalesRabbit.

TIP:The old way of creating leads is still available in the updated version of SalesRabbit.

heading: Part 1: Previous: Lead Creation
body:
Review of creating leads in the previous version of SalesRabbit.

- Previous lead creation required users to select the pin icon in the cluster of icons on the right-hand side of the map in the SalesHub.
- After selecting the pin icon, a "Lead Menu" would appear at the bottom of the screen.
- Then, users had to select the lead status option from the lead menu and then tap the home they wanted to pin the lead status to.
- After that the lead status icon would appear of the house and the address would be recorded.

heading: Part 2: Update: Long Press Lead Creation
body:
Utilizing the long press feature to create leads in the updated version of SalesRabbit.

- In the updated version of SalesRabbit, leads can be pinned to a home without using the pin icon.
- Simply navigate to the desired home or location on your map in the SalesHub on the mobile app.
- Once you have found the desired home or location, just tap and hold your finger on the location.
- A wheel of the lead status icon will appear around the selected home.
  - Note : the first 10 listed statuses on your workspace's Lead Status page will appear as options in the Long Press wheel .

- Select the desired status and the lead status icon will appear over the home.
  - The address will be recorded the same way it is when using the pin icon.

heading: Part 2: Schedule an Appointment for Yourself
body:
This part will walk users through scheduling an appointment "for yourself" using advanced appointment management on the mobile app.

- From the mobile app, navigate to " SalesHub " and select on the lead you'd like to schedule an appointment for.
- Open that lead's information card by selecting " Details ".

- It's best practice for users to add necessary lead information (first name, last name, phone, email...) to the lead card before scheduling an appointment.
- Navigate to the appointment section toward the bottom of lead card and select " Set Appointment " -> " For Myself ".
  - Note: Selecting "For Myself" allows the user to schedule an appointment directly to the calendar that they've connected. Selecting "For Others" allows users to schedule on another user's calendar.

- After choosing " For Myself ", the user will then see a calendar view displaying times their calendar says they're available for an appointment.
- View available time slots for each day by selecting on a specific day.
- The default scheduled meeting length is 1hr.
  - Users can adjust the scheduled meeting time length by selecting the time and choosing how long they'd like the appointment to be.

heading: Part 1: Managing Roles
body:
This part will cover how to create, rename, and delete roles in your workspace.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App , navigate to " Settings " -> click " Roles & Permissions ".

- The left side of the Roles & Permission will list the workspace's available Roles.
  - Note : for new workspaces, there will be 4 default roles available (Owner, Admin, Manager, and Rep) .

- Users can can add, delete, edit, rename, and rearrange the hierarchy/order of these roles as need.

- Clicking " Add Role " allows users to create a new role.
- Name the new role -> click " Create " to add it to your list of existing roles.
  - Note : in the example below, we have created a new role called "New Role".

- After selecting an existing role, an " Actions " button will be on the right side of the screen, allowing users to " Edit Detail s" (the name) for that role, or to " Delete Role ".
  - Note : deleting a role requires that you reassign users of that role to a new role .

heading: Part 2: Editing Role Permissions
body:
This section will cover how to adjust the permission set for a specific role(s). A user's role ultimately determines what that user can do and see within a SaleRabbit+ workspace.
Note: a user's role permissions will apply to their current Team Assignment (and associated sub-teams), but not to teams the user does not have access to in the workspace.

- To edit the permissions for a role, navigate to " Settings " -> select " Roles & Permissions " -> select a role to edit.
- To the right of the list of roles will be a list of permissions for the role you've chosen.
- The listed permissions will have a checkbox(es) to the right, allowing users to determine whether or not the selected role has that permission enabled.
  - View Permission Checkbox :
    - Allow users to view or access certain information or features.

  - Manage Permission Checkbox :
    - Allow users to make changes, edit, or control certain aspects of the system.

- After editing a role's permissions, be sure to click " Save " in the bottom right corner to apply any changes made.

heading: Article Overview
body: This article will demonstrate the basics of creating, assigning, and editing areas in the SR+ mobile app. SalesRabbit Areas is a powerful tool designed to streamline and enhance the management of sales territories. At its core, the product addresses the common challenges associated with area management, such as inefficient territory assignments, lack of clarity in sales targets, and difficulties in tracking performance across different regions. The primary problem that area management solves is the optimization of sales efforts by ensuring that each sales representative (Rep) is assigned a clearly defined territory to work within. This reduces overlap, maximizes coverage, and ensures that all potential leads within a given area are effectively addressed. Additionally, it provides a structured framework for tracking sales activities and performance metrics within each area, enabling more informed decision-making and strategic planning. SalesRabbit Areas caters to two distinct user groups: Managers and Reps. Managers are responsible for creating and assigning areas, ensuring that territories are strategically defined and aligned with the company's sales goals.

heading: Article Overview
body: SalesRabbit Areas caters to two distinct user groups: Managers and Reps. Managers are responsible for creating and assigning areas, ensuring that territories are strategically defined and aligned with the company's sales goals. They utilize the tool to monitor area performance, reassign territories as needed, and optimize resource allocation to maximize sales potential. On the other hand, Reps are the individuals who are assigned these areas to work. For Reps, SalesRabbit Areas provides clarity on their specific responsibilities and targets within their designated territories, allowing them to focus their efforts and track their progress effectively. Through the dual focus on Managers and Reps, SalesRabbit Areas facilitates a more organized and efficient sales process, ultimately driving better results and a more cohesive sales strategy. TIP:The ability to create/view other user's areas will depend on your role's permissions.

heading: Part 1: Areas Permission
body:
This part will explain the permissions associated with area management. Permissions are managed on the Web App.
Note: users with these permissions can create/assign areas for users who are on or below their assigned team.

- In order for a user to create/edit areas, that user must have the view & manage "Areas" permission enabled for their role .
- To edit a roles' permissions, navigate to " Settings " -> " Roles & Permissions " in the web app .
  - Select the role you'd like to edit and enable both " View " and " Manage ".

- Available Area permissions include:
  - Areas : draw out territories and assign them to users to work leads in that specific area.
    - View: allows users at that role to view other team member's assigned areas on the map.
    - Manage: allows users at that role to create/assign fellow team members to areas.

  - Area Activity : view area performance metrics and engagement data to analyze territory effectiveness.
  - Area Settings : allows users to limit assigned areas per user and set automatic removal after inactivity.

- If making changes to a role's permission set, don't forget to click " Save " in the bottom right corner.

heading: Part 2: Create an Area
body:
This part will demonstrate how to create and assign areas in the mobile app.

- Areas can be created with the " Lasso Tool " on the SalesHub Map.
- The Lasso Tool can be found on the upper left side of the map.

- Selecting the lasso tool will allow a user to circle around a neighborhood or area using their finger.
- Once the shape is complete, a " New Area " creation drawer will appear at the bottom.
- To create an area:
  - Name or give the area a "Title" (optional).
  - Select the Team the area will be assigned to.
  - Assign the area to a user(s) from the selected team.
  - Click " Create " to assign the area.

- Note: Lassoing an area with leads on the map will not automatically create an area. Instead you'll select the "Create Area" icon.

Zapier allow users to connect apps and automate workflows. It's easy automation for busy people. Zapier enables customers to create and manage their own integrations through Zapier when our integration Marketplace does not meet their specific needs. Zapier's low-code interface provides a user-friendly option for less technical customers to build automations without requiring developer support.
A Zapier automation can help remove the process of double entry or importing/exporting data between your utilized software. heading: Part 2: Map Your Statuses to Stages
body:
This part will cover how to map your lead statuses to specific Amplify Stages.

- Mapping statuses to an Amplify Stage can be done when creating or editing a lead status .
- Navigate to "Settings" -> "Lead Statuses" in the Web App.

- Select the lead status you'd like to edit the stage for (or create a new lead status).
- A pop-out will appear on the right hand side with an option to change the "Amplify Stage" for that status.

heading: Part 3: Using Proximity Indicator (Mobile App)
body:
In this section, we show how to use Proximity Indicator to check the locations of Reps when leads updated.

- From the SalesRabbit+ mobile app, click on the " SalesHub " section to access the mobile app map.
- After following the steps in Part 1 & 2 of this article, small icon bubbles will appear in the upper right corner of each lead on the SalesHub Map.
- These indicator icon bubbles indicate if the rep was:
  - At Location (within 25m): Green Checkmark (√) .
  - Near Location (within 25m-100m): Yellow Checkmark (√) .
  - Out of Range ( >100m): Red Exclamation Point (!) .
  - Unknown Location : Grey Question Mark (?) .
    - Typically appears on recently imported leads, the lead was created from the Web App, or the user's location is unable to be determined.

- To check the exact location of the rep for a specific lead, select you lead you wish to see that info for, then click details from the pop up.

- Once on the details page, click " Activity " in the top right hand corner.
- Finally, lick the logged event that you would like to check the location for.

- A new pop-up will appear letting you know if the user was in or out of range for when performing the selected event.

In this section, we show how to use Proximity Indicator to check the locations of Reps when leads updated.

- From the SalesRabbit+ mobile app, click on the " SalesHub " section to access the mobile app map.
- After following the steps in Part 1 & 2 of this article, small icon bubbles will appear in the upper right corner of each lead on the SalesHub Map.
- These indicator icon bubbles indicate if the rep was:
  - At Location (within 25m): Green Checkmark (√) .
  - Near Location (within 25m-100m): Yellow Checkmark (√) .
  - Out of Range ( >100m): Red Exclamation Point (!) .
  - Unknown Location : Grey Question Mark (?) .
    - Typically appears on recently imported leads, the lead was created from the Web App, or the user's location is unable to be determined.

- To check the exact location of the rep for a specific lead, select you lead you wish to see that info for, then click details from the pop up.

- Once on the details page, click " Activity " in the top right hand corner.
- Finally, lick the logged event that you would like to check the location for.

- A new pop-up will appear letting you know if the user was in or out of range for when performing the selected event.
title: Proximity Indicator

heading: Part 2: Filtering Options
body:
This part will cover what each filtering option is capable of. Selecting the upside down carrot icon will give you the ability to be specific with each filter. Be sure to select "Apply" once your filters are set.

- My Leads Filter:
  - This filter will manage leads where the user is the lead owner (your leads).
  - This filter allows the user to filter for their leads that were created/updated within a specified date range, or select specifically which statuses they want to appear on the SalesHub Map.

- Others Leads Filter:
  - This filter will manage leads where the user is not the lead owner (other user's leads).
  - A user with access to this filter will be able to choose which users leads they'd like to view, filter for leads created/updated within a specified date range, or select specifically which statuses they want to appear on the SalesHub Map.
  - This filter is available to users whose role has the permission to View Others Leads.
    - Note : this filter is available to users whose role has the "View Others Leads" permission enabled.

- DataGrid AI Filter:
  - If an account has the DataGrid AI add-on, then a DataGrid filter will also appear.

heading: Part 1: Lead Status Permission
body:
This part demonstrates how to edit a user's role to allow for viewing/managing a workspace's lead statuses.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App , navigate to " Settings " -> " Roles & Permissions ".
- Select the " Role " you'd like to edit the lead status permission for.
- Under the " General " list of permissions, the " Lead Status " permission allows for:
  - View : allows users of that role to view available lead status on the Web App.
  - Manage : allows users assigned to the role the ability to create/edit/delete the available lead statuses for the workspace.

- Click " Save " to apply any changes made.

heading: Part 2: Accessing Lead Statuses
body:
This part will detail how to access a list of your lead statuses from Web and mobile.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App , navigate to " Settings " -> " Lead Statuses "
- The Lead Status page provides options to view a list of Active and Deactivated lead statuses. Active lead statuses will be available for all users in the workspace to use from the mobile app.
  - Note : the first 10 statuses listed will be available with the long press !

- From the Mobile App, all users, regardless of role, users can access a list of their workspaces active lead statuses by selecting the "i" icon next to the lead status section on a lead details page.

heading: Part 3: Create/Edit a Lead Status
body:
This part details how to create a new lead status and edit an existing lead status.

- To create a new lead status, select the " Create " button in the upper right hand corner.

- After selecting " Create ", a pop-out will appear on the right hand of the screen.
- Provide the following information for the new status:
  - Status Name : provide a name for the new status.
  - Abbreviation : provide a 4 character abbrevation.
  - Amplify Stage : assign the status to count toward an Amplify Stage .
  - Color : select a color to represent the status.
  - Icon : select an icon to represent the status.
  - Locked Lead Setting : turn the status into a "Locked" lead status.
    - Tip : visit the Locked Lead article for more information regarding locked statuses .

- After completing the status details, select " Save " in the bottom right.

- The new status will be added at the bottom of the list of Active Lead Statuses.
- To edit an existing lead status, select the lead status and the same editing side bar will appear on the right hand side.
- Rearrange the list of statuses by selecting the three bar icon on the left side to click and drag that status to it's desired position/rank.

heading: Part 4: Deactivate/Delete a Lead Status
body:
This part will detail how to deactivate/delete an active lead status.

- Deactivate a lead status by selecting the three dots on the right hand side and selecting " Deactivate ".
  - Note : Deactivating a lead status will not delete or reassign leads currently set to that status. Rather, it means that users are no longer able to assign leads to the deactivated status .

- A list of deactivated status are listed under the " Deactivated " tab on the main Lead Status page.
- Reactivate a status by selecting the three dots icon for the status and selecting " Reactivate ".
- Reactivated statuses will now appear as an option on the Active Lead Statuses list.

- Note : deleting a lead status will require that leads of that status are assigned to a new status .

heading: Part 5: Locked Lead Statuses
body:
Locked Lead Statuses are a powerful new feature in SalesRabbit+ that enables organizations to create and manage 'view only' leads across their entire sales force.

- Enhanced Territory Management: Teams can mark and identify customer locations and "do-not-contact" addresses that are visible to all relevant team members.
- Location-based Intelligence: Sales Reps can only see locked leads within a specified radius, regardless of lead ownership, improving field efficiency.
- Data Protection: Organizations can control what lead information is displayed (name only, name and address, or no details) to maintain Privacy and compliance.

- Locked Leads Permissions
  - The ability to view/manage locked leads on the map is dependent on a user's Role .
  - You can edit a user's role permissions by navigating to " Settings " -> " Roles " -> selecting the role you'd like to edit this permission for.
  - The permission is called " Locked Leads " and can be found under the "Leads" section.
    - The "View" permission allows the user the ability to view locked statuses on their mobile/web map within a defined radius.
    - The "Manage" permission allows a user at that role the ability to create/manage locked lead statuses.

- Locked Lead Settings
  - Leads marked with a locked status will be visible to all users within a defined radius of the user's current physical location.

heading: Part 2: Obtain Webhook URL
body:
Note: for demo purposes, we will be creating a Zap that adds a row to a spreadsheet when a lead is updated to an "Appointment" lead status.

- From your Zapier account, click " Create " -> " Zaps ".

- Click the " Trigger " step -> use the text field to search for " Webhooks " by Zapier.

- Within the trigger setup, use the " Trigger Event " dropdown to select the " Catch Hook " option.
- Click " Continue " to move to the configure step.

- Within the trigger configure step, a child key is not necessary. Click " Continue " to bypass this page.

- Within the trigger test step, " Copy " the generated webhook URL.
- This webhook URL will be pasted in a location in your SalesRabbit+ account.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App, navigate to " Integrations " -> " Webhooks " -> click " Create Webhook ".

- From the right hand pop-out, enter in the following information:
  - Title : name the webhook.
  - URL : "Paste" the copied URL from Zapier.
  - Event Type : select the event you'd like to trigger the webhooks.
    - Forms :
      - Form Submitted: triggers when a form is submitted from the lead.

    - Leads :
      - Lead Created: triggers when a lead is created and marked with a designated status(es).
      - Lead Updated: triggers when a lead is updated (contact info, custom fields, status update, etc.)
      - Lead Deleted: triggers when a lead is deleted.
      - Lead Status Updated: triggers when a lead's status is updated to a designated status(es).
      - Lead Owner Modified: triggers when a lead's owner is updated.

    - Areas :
      - Area Created: triggers when an area is created.
      - Area Updated: triggers when an area is updated.
      - Area Deleted: triggers when an area is deleted.

  - Event Sub-Type : select the status(es) that a lead must be set to for the webhook to trigger.

- Click " Create " when finished.
  - Note : in the below example, the webhook will trigger when a lead's status is updated to the "Appointment Set" lead status .

- Next, test the trigger in Zapier.
- Before proceeding, create one or two test leads that meet the requirements of the new Zap.
  - For example, in this article, we've set up a webhook that triggers when a lead is marked with the "Appointment Set" lead status.

heading: Part 1: What is a Metric?
body:
Amplify offers a number of fields for storing data. If you use a combination of activities, number fields, and dropdown options, it can be a challenge to set the correct data filter every time you are configuring a widget, slide, competition, achievement to visualize and measure progress for your KPIs.
Metrics work as a common recipe for how to retrieve KPIs from Amplify. If you define your KPIs in metrics, you can set up your slides and widgets to use the metric instead of setting the correct combination of fields and options every time you add new content to your dashboards.

heading: Part 2: Create a New Metric
body:
This part will demonstrate how to create a new Metric in Amplify.

- Login to Amplify on a desktop -> click " Manage " -> " Metrics ".

- This page allows users to view their active/usable metrics. The metrics on this page can be used to report inside of widget on your dashboard, competitions, and achievements.
- To create a new metric, click " + New Metric " in the upper right corner.

- You'll be shown a " New Metric " creation page.
- On this page, users can:
  - Name the metric and add a description (optional)
    - Note : Users can also create a "Tag" for each metric, allowing you to organize, label, and filter your metrics by.

  - Select which " Activity Type " to base this metric on:
    - Each metric is based on a specific Activity Type that you choose.
      - Lead Status : will give credit to the user who creates/updates the status of a lead in SalesRabbit.
      - Resulting Status : will give credit to the setter when a closer updates the status of an existing lead in SalesRabbit.

    - Note : the most commonly used activity type is "Lead Status".

  - Under " Activities ", select which lead status from SalesRabbit you'd like this metric to count or keep track of.
    - Users will receive credit toward a metric when they mark a lead with one of the selected statuses.

  - Under " Proximity ", choose whether you'd like the user to receive credit based on whether the user is At Location, Near Location, Not at Location, or if Unknown will count.
  - Select " Continue to Formula ".

- Choose whether you'd like this metric to display as a:
  - Sum : will display the total sum of your selected number field.
    - This sums up the value based on the field you select in “Measured in.” This is similar to when you selected “Value” as a function when creating a widget.
    - You can select among all the value fields from the selected “Activity Type”

  - Average : will calculate the average value per report.
    - This takes the sum of the “Measured in” field you select and divides it by number of reports (this is not the same as sum of quantity as before).
    - This differs from the "average" function used in widgets, competitions, etc.
      - For example:

  - Division : will divide one number by another.

heading: Part 4: What is a Tag?
body:
We know that it can be hard to organize things when you have a high number of metrics in an account. Tags are meant to help simplify that. Use them to identify a purpose or supplemental information about a metric, like info about integrations that add data for this metric, which roles uses it, or anything else you can think of that might be relevant for your setup.

- If a metric has an attached tag, it will be listed under the manage metrics screen.
- Tags can be added to a metric by editing that metric.

- Select " Manage Tags " to create/edit available tags.

- To edit an existing tag, select the three dot icon to the right of the listed tag.
- To create a new tag, click " + New Tag ".

Pro Tips

- Metrics are the basis of everything in Amplify. They are tracked inside of widgets on your dashboards, in competitions, and toward achievements.
- If a widget on your dashboard is reporting an incorrect number, double check that the metric reporting in that widget has been set up properly.

heading: Article Overview
body:
Locked Leads is a powerful new feature in SalesRabbit+ that enables organizations to create and manage 'view only' leads across their entire sales force.

- Enhanced Territory Management: Teams can mark and identify customer locations and do-not-contact addresses that are visible to all relevant team members.
- Location-based Intelligence: Sales Reps can see nearby leads within a specific radius, regardless of lead ownership, improving field efficiency.
- Data Protection: Organizations can control what information is displayed (name only, name and address, or no detail) to maintain privacy and compliance.
TIP: Locked Leads are permission based. Please reach out to your Admin, Owner, or Manager about this permission.

- Data Protection: Organizations can control what information is displayed (name only, name and address, or no detail) to maintain privacy and compliance.

heading: Part 1: Locked Leads Permissions
body:
Configuring Roles & Permissions for Locked Leads.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App, navigate to " Settings " -> then select " Roles & Permissions ".
- Once in Roles, find the Locked Lead permission under the Leads section.
- Go through each Role and enable/disable the View or Manage permission.
  - View Permission : allows the role the ability to view Locked Leads on Web/Mobile.
  - Manage Permission : allows the role to edit leads marked with a Locked Lead status.

- Remember to select " Save " if making changes.
