heading: Part 2: Manage Locked Lead Statuses
body:
Creating/Choosing which lead statuses will be Locked.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App, navigate to " Settings " -> select " Lead Statuses ".
- Click " Create " in the upper left corner.
  - Tip : users can edit an existing status and change it to a Locked Lead Status.

- To create a locked lead status, fill out the following information in the right hand side bar:
  - Status Name : provide a status name.
  - Abbreviation : provide a 4 character status abbreviation.
  - Amplify Stage : select the status' Amplify stage.
  - Color : choose the status color.
  - Icon : select an icon to represent the status.

heading: Article Overview
body: Users are able to create and manage effective routes for batches of leads from the SalesRabbit+ Mobile App.
text:
Mobile App > Routing - Mobile App :: Article Overview

Users are able to create and manage effective routes for batches of leads from the SalesRabbit+ Mobile App.
title: Routing - Mobile App

heading: Part 1: Create a Route
body:
This part will demonstrate how to create a route in the SalesRabbit+ Mobile App.

- After logging into the SalesRabbit+ mobile app, navigate to " SalesHub " -> select the double pin " Route " icon in the upper left corner of the map.

- This page will display a list of previously created routes that you can manage.
- To create a new route, select the " + " icon in the upper right corner.

- Users will be brought to a routing page where they can fill in the following fields of information:
- Route Nam e : name your new route.
  - Note : the default name will always be today's date.

- Start/End Points : enter in the address of where you'd like this route to begin and the address of where you'd like to end.
  - Note : select the target icon on the far right end of the row to pull the address for your current location.

- Stops : users are able to select the leads they'd like to include on a route as "stops".
  - To add leads or "stops" to a route, select " Add Leads ".

- Filter for the leads you'd like to include on a route.
- In the below example, there is no date range applied, but we are searching for leads of a specific status (NH, APPT, FOLU).
- After setting the criteria, select " Next ".

- A list of leads based on your search criteria will appear.
- Select the leads you'd like to add as stops -> " Add ".
  - Note : there is a cap of 23 leads/stops that can be added to a single route.

- The selected leads will be added as stops on your routing page.
- More stops can be added to an existing route by selecting " Add Leads ".

- Optimization Options : enabling any of these options will be applied to your route.

- Click " Start " in the upper right corner to view the route on the map.
- That route's information will appear with summary of the route's distance, driving time, and number of stops.
  - Note : toggling " Show Route Only " on will only display the stops along the selected route.

- Each stop on the route will have a number appear in the upper left corner.

heading: Part 2: Create and Manage Areas on the Web App
body:
This part will demonstrate how to create and manage areas on the Web App map.

- First, navigate to the location you would like to create an area for.
- Select the " Draw Area " icon in the upper left corner.
  - You cursor will turn into a " + " symbol. Create a starting point by clicking on the map -> move your mouse and click, dropping a new point -> move your mouse and click again until you complete your area.
  - Upon completing the area's shape, it will turn your user's assigned color, and an area creation page will appear on the right side.
  - Options to include when creating an area are:
    - Area Name (optional): give this newly drawn area a name.
    - Team : select which team/sub-team this area will be assigned to.
    - Assigned to : select which user(s) to assign this area.
    - Color : choose a color to represent this area on the map.

  - Click " Create " in the bottom right corner to create your new area.

- Selecting an existing area with leads will display an area overview, detailing how many leads have been created vs. how many homes are in the area with a percentage complete.

- Additionally, users can edit an area's name, team/user assignment and color under " Info " in the right menu.

- And view historical area activity/recent updates.

- If making edits to an area, don't forget to click " Save "!

heading: Part 4: Bulk Reassign Leads
body:
This part will cover how to Bulk Select and Reassign leads in the Web App. Reassigning Leads without a Knocking Area

- First select the " Bulk Select " cursor below the Area Creation icon.
- This will turn your cursor into a " + " symbol and allow you to lasso the leads you wish to reassign.
- Use your mouse to click and drag around the leads you want to reassign:
- After drawing the shape, a new right side menu will appear.
- The new menu displays how many leads were selected, their statuses, and a dropdown to select the Org Assignment and User you are going to reassign the leads to.
- To reassign ownership of these leads from one user to another, select a user with the dropdown menu -> click the " Apply " button on the bottom right side of the menu.
- A loading bar will appear, followed by a green " Success " check mark indicating the leads have been reassigned to the new user.

- Tip : users can reassign leads and perform other bulk actions by selecting a knocking area .
- Navigate to the user's knocking area you wish to reassign leads from.
- Click on the area and you will see the option that says " Select Leads " in the pop up menu on the right-hand side of the screen.

- After clicking " Select Leads ", the page of all of the leads in the area will appear, all leads will be selected, to unselect the leads simply click on the check mark on the top left.

heading: Part 5: Map Filters
body:
This part will cover how the map filters affect the information appearing on the Web App map.

- The map filters can be found at the top of the map.
- These filtering options provide users with an opportunity to view leads on the map that meet a specified criteria.
  - Options to filter leads for include:
    - Lead Status : displays leads of a select status(es).
    - Assigned To : displays leads that are owned by a chosen user(s).
    - Date Created : displays leads that were created within a specified date range.
    - Date Updated : displays leads that were updated within a specified date range.
    - Appointment : displays leads with a scheduled appointment within a specified date range.
    - Campaigns : displays leads assigned to selected campaigns .
    - Custom Fields : displays leads that meet set custom field criteria.

  - Click " Apply " in the bottom right corner for your filters to take effect.
  - If a filter has been applied, you'll see a notification in the filter icon at the top of the map.

  - Clear any set filters by selecting " Clear All " -> " Apply " in your filtering options.

- TIP: If you feel you are missing leads from the map, double check your filters and your role's permissions!

heading: Part 6: Map Layers
body:
This part will cover how to upload and manage map overlays on the Web App map. Note: the ability to view and manage map overlays is dependent on your assigned role.

- The " Map Layers " can be found at the bottom of the icons on the left side of the SalesHub Map.
- When selected, a right hand pop-out will appear.

- Enable the " User Locations " toggle to view your users most recent location on the map.
- Under overlays, click " Add Overlay " to upload an overlay to the map.
  - When adding an overlay, click and drag the " File " into the right pop-out.
  - Name the overlay in the " Title " field.
  - Under " Visibility ", select who has access to view the overlay (All, Teams, or Individuals).
  - Note : supported file types include KML, KMZ, SHP, GEOJSON. Maximum file size: 5MB. Limit of 100 overlays.

- After uploading an overlay, use the checkbox to the left of an overlay to display on the map.
  - Note : uploaded map overlays are also visible from the mobile app to users with the appropriate access. Pro Tips

- Some map functions (area creation) will depend on your user's Role .
- Information that comes with DataGrid AI is not currently available on the Web App.

heading: Article Overview
body: SalesRabbit Areas is a powerful tool designed to streamline and enhance the management of sales territories. At its core, the product addresses the common challenges associated with area management, such as inefficient territory assignments, lack of clarity in sales targets, and difficulties in tracking performance across different regions. The primary problem that area management solves is the optimization of sales efforts by ensuring that each sales representative (Rep) is assigned a clearly defined territory to work within. This reduces overlap, maximizes coverage, and ensures that all potential leads within a given area are effectively addressed. Additionally, it provides a structured framework for tracking sales activities and performance metrics within each area, enabling more informed decision-making and strategic planning. SalesRabbit Areas caters to two distinct user groups: Managers and Reps. Managers are responsible for creating and assigning areas, ensuring that territories are strategically defined and aligned with the company's sales goals.

heading: Part 3: Create an Area on Web
body:
This part will cover how to create areas on the SalesRabbit+ Web App. Note: areas can also be created from the SalesRabbit Mobile App.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App, navigate to " SalesHub " -> " Map ".

- Zoom in over the area on the map you'd like to create an area for and select the " Area Creation Tool " in the upper left corner of the map.
- Area creation has two mode: Polygon Mode and Freehand Mode.

- Polygon Mode :
  - Used for precise, point-by-point area creation and lead selection.
  - When selected, create various points by clicking around the desired area and complete the shape.

- Freehand Mode :
  - Used for quick, natural drawing gestures.
  - When selected, click once -> drag your mouse around the area you'd like to create -> click again once finished.

- Once you complete the area boundaries, a right side " Create Area " menu.

heading: Part 4: Edit an Area on Web
body:
This part will cover how to edit and manage existing areas on the SalesRabbit+ Web App.

- From the SalesHub Map on the Web, select an existing area.
- A menu will appear on the right side, displaying that area's " Overview ". The overview contains information on how many leads there are vs. the number of homes existing within the area. Additionally, a breakdown of how many leads of each status existing in the area.

- Under the " Info " tab, users who can manage areas may update the area name, team assignment, user assignment, and color.

- Under " Activity ", users will see a historical list of changes made to the selected area.

- Additionally, users with the manage area permission enabled can " Delete " an existing area.

- If attempting to delete an area, a confirmation pop-out will appear asking to confirm the action.
- Deleting an area will only delete the drawn boundaries. Lead information is not deleted.

Pro Tips

- Areas can also be created/managed from the mobile app .
- At this time, add-on information (DataGrid) is only visible from the map on the mobile app.

heading: Article Overview
body:
One of the primary ways SalesRabbit improves sales processes is by helping users collect accurate lead information. The more a sales team knows about their leads, the more effectively they can move them through the pipeline.
While SalesRabbit offers a variety of generic fields out of the box, some teams require more specific data in order to do their job effectively, which is why we offer Custom Fields.
With Custom Fields, you can create customized fields that will display on the Lead Detail page, so your team can collect the exact information that is needed to make a sale.
TIP:Custom Fields are currently available to Pro accounts or higher.

heading: Part 1: Custom Field Permissions
body:
This part will explain the permissions that must be enabled for a user to manage custom fields.

- Whether a user can manage custom fields will depend on their Role's permissions.
- To edit a role's permissions, Navigate to " Settings " -> " Roles & Permissions " -> Select the role you'd like to edit in the Web App.
- The " Custom Field " permission is found under the Leads category.
  - View Permission: selecting the view checkbox will enable a user at that role to view created custom fields on the Web App.
  - Manage Permission: selecting the manage checkbox enables a user at that role to create/edit custom fields for your account.

- Don't forget to select " Save " if you make any changes to the role's permissions.
- Note: these permissions only deal with actions on the Web App. All users will be able to view created custom fields on the mobile app regardless of what their roles permissions are.

heading: Part 2: Creating a Custom Field
body:
This part will demonstrate how to create a custom field for your account.

- From the Web App, navigate to " Settings " -> " Custom Fields ".
- There are different types of Custom Fields that can be created.
- To create a Custom Fields, select " Add Field " in the upper right corner.

- A drawer will appear on the right hand side, allowing you to give the custom field a name and select what type of field you wish to create.
- Field Type options include:
  - Short Text Field (searchable) : allows for up to 255 characters in a text field.
    - Example: Spouse name (two contacts)

  - Long Text Field (searchable) : allows for up to 2500 characters in a text field.

  - Dropdown (filter-able) : create a drop-down list of answers that a user can choose from (up to 100 options) Example: House Type - Apt, Townhouse, etc.
    - Select " + Add Option " to add options to select.
    - Enable " Multi-Select " to allow your user to select more than one option.
      - Example: Service Interest - Such as: solar, roof, siding, etc.
      - You can also choose single select.

  - Date (filterable) : creates a new field to select a specific date.
    - Example: Warranty Expiration - Day/Month/Year, or Date of Storm - Day/Month/Year

  - Date & Time (currently not filterable) : creates a new field to enter in both a date and select a time.

- Time (filter-able) : Choose a singular time.
  - Example: Best Return Time: 6:30 PM

- Number (filterable) : Greater than or equal to zero.
  - Example: House square footage

- Currency (filterable): Formatted in USD ($).
  - Example: Estimate

- Phone (searchable): Phone Number.
  - Example: Spouses Phone Number

- Email (searchable): Email Address.
  - Example: Spouses email

  - Note: More Field types will be added as they become available.

- Depending on the field type you select, you'll also be presented with the following options:
  - View Only toggle: toggling this on will make the custom field visible but not editable.

heading: Part 1: Browsing Reports
body:
This part will demonstrate how to browse existing reports within Amplify.

- To access historical reports, click on " Reports " in the left side menu.
- Each time a user creates or updates the status of a lead, a line item called a Report is generated within Amplify.
- A Report documents which user updated a lead, what status it was updated to, provides a SalesRabbit Lead ID, lists the user's proximity, and provides the date/time that lead was updated.
- These reports feed the data reporting within metrics on the Dashboard.
- From the " Reports " tab, users are able to Browse, Add, Edit, and Delete created Reports.

heading: Part 2: Report Filters
body:

- Type and Date Range Filters:
  - Activity Type : select the type of reports you're searching for.
    - Note : visit our article on Activity Types for more information.

  - Period : select a default period (today, last 7 days, current month...).
  - From/To : set a custom date range.
  - Group By : set a grouping.

- Specific Report filters:
  - User : filter for reports belonging to a specific user(s).
  - Department : filter reports by department(s).
  - Team : filter reports by team(s) assignment.
  - Activity : filter reports by the Lead Status listed in SalesRabbit.
  - Lead Name : search reports by a Lead Name.
  - SalesRabbit ID : search reports by the SalesRabbit ID.
  - Proximity : filter reports by the proximity status.
    - Note : options include At Location, Near Location, Not at Location, or Unknown.

- After filtering for specific reports, users can select " More Actions " and perform actions like Importing/Export from or to Excel and Batch Delete Reports.

heading: Part 3: Adding Reports
body:
This part demonstrates how to manually add a Report to amplify.

- From the Amplify Reports tab, click " + Add " in the upper right corner.

- Enter in the following information:
  - User : the user that should receive credit.
  - Type : select the type of report (Lead Status is the default Type).
  - Activity : select the Lead Status that was marked.
  - Quantity : choose the quantity.
  - SalesRabbit Lead ID : enter in the SalesRabbit Lead ID.
    - Note : users can access a lead's ID from the SR Lead page and inspecting the URL.

  - Proximity : choose the proximity for the report.

- Click " Add Report " to save and add the historical report.

heading: Part 4: Editing Reports
body:
Typically, reports will detail the pure details of what happened. Depending on the Activity Type, you'll see details for who made the change, what status was updated, what lead the change affected, and when the change occurred.

- To edit details on an existing report, simply select on the detail field.
- Fields that can be edited include Lead Name, SalesRabbit Lead ID, Proximity, Date/Time, and Quantity.
  - Note : if a report is incorrect, it may be necessary to delete the existing report and create a new report with the correct details.

- Click " Save Changes " in the bottom right corner.

- To bulk edit multiple reports at once, filter for the desired reports -> check the box for the report(s) -> click " Edit ".

- Fields that user are able to edit in bulk can be selected and adjusted from this pop-out.
  - Note : in most cases, "Quantity" will be the only option users can update in bulk.

- Click " Continue " to apply your changes.

heading: Part 5: Deleting Reports
body:
This part demonstrates how to manually delete a report(s) in Amplify.

- You can delete an individual report by click the three dot icon to the right of a report -> clicking " Delete ".
- The easiest way to delete multiple reports at once is to filter for the desired reports -> use the check box to select the reports -> click " Delete Selected ".

- When deleting leads, users will be asked to confirm the action.
- Click " Delete " to confirm.

- User can also delete multiple leads at once by setting the filters for the desired leads -> selecting " More Actions " -> click " Batch Delete Reports ".
- CAUTION : this action has the ability to delete ALL reports.

- A prompt asking to confirm the action will appear.
- This action will delete all reports that match the set filters and CANNOT be undone. Connected entities, such as coins and XP, will also be deleted.
- Confirm the number of reports to delete -> click " Delete ".

heading: Part 2: New Area Management
body:
This part quickly demonstrates how to create/manage areas on the next generation of SalesRabbit.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App , navigate to " SalesHub " -> click " Map ".
- The "Draw Area" icon now lives in the upper left corner of the map.

- In the next generation of SalesRabbit, there are two methods when it comes to creating new areas on the Web App:
  - Polygon Mode : create areas using the mouse to click points around the area boundaries.
    - Click the " Draw Area " icon in the upper left corner -> select " Polygon Mode ".
    - Use the mouse to click points to create the new area boundaries.
    - After completing the shape, an " Create Area " menu will appear, allowing users to add an Area Name, assign the area to a Team, and assign the area to a member of the selected team.

- Freehand Mode : draw areas freely using the mouse.
  - Click the " Draw Area " icon in the upper left corner -> select " Freehand Mode ".
  - Click the mouse once, then freely move the mouse to draw the new area boundaries.
  - Click again to complete the area shape.
  - After completing the shape, a " Create Area " menu will appear, allowing users to add an Area Name, assign the area to a Team, and assign the area to a member of the selected team.

- Don't forget to click the " Create " button for your new area assignment to be created.
- Users will be notified in the mobile app when a new area is assigned to them.

heading: Article Overview
body:
This guide outlines the steps to create a Scorecard in Amplify. From initial setup to defining objectives and activities, assigning benchmarks, and viewing created scorecards are essential for tracking team and individual progress toward objectives.
With scorecards, it is possible to visualize different activities together, define the relation/weight between them, and visualize the progress toward company objectives. This will bring insight in how you and your colleagues are performing, and where the effort should be to increase the score. The perfect score is 100 in the end of the period.
TIP:Amplify Scorecards are only to available to Pro/Enterprise accounts. Additionally, users must have admin access within Amplify to create/manage Scorecards. If you'd like to have scorecards enabled, please reach out to the SalesRabbit Support Team.

heading: Part 1: Scorecard Setup
body:
This part will cover how to perform the initial scorecard setup within Amplify.

- From Amplify on the web, navigate to " Scorecards " in the left menu -> click " Get Started ".

- If this is your first time setting up a scorecard, you'll be brought to the Scorecard Settings screen.
- In these settings:
  - Company vs. Team Scorecards:
    - Company: if you want a scorecard defined for every user in the company.
    - Team: if you want a scorecard defined for every team in the company.

  - Primary Objective Score (required):
    - Prove a Name for your primary scorecard.
    - Select the default Period to track performance (weekly, monthly, quarterly).
    - Set the Privacy level for the scorecard, i.e. who can view others' scorecards.

  - Secondary Objective Score (optional):
    - Use the toggle to generate a second scorecard.

  - Click " Save " to continue scorecard setup.

- After the initial setup, users will be able to edit Scorecard settings by selecting " Scorecards " -> clicking " Edit Scorecards " -> " Settings ".

heading: Part 2: Manage Scorecards
body:
This part will demonstrate how to manage/create a new scorecard.

- After selecting " Edit Scorecard ", select the scorecard you'd like to edit -> use the " + Create " button to begin adding metrics to your set scorecard.

- Select the " + " -> " Select Metric " to begin adding metrics to track on the desired scorecard.

- Select the metric(s) you'd like to add -> " Save ".
- Follow the same steps to add as many metrics as you'd like to track on the scorecard.

- After adding metrics to the dashboard, users are able to assign a default Benchmark and a Weight percentage.
  - Benchmark : the default goal to each Amplify user to achieve for that metric.
  - Weight : set a weight percent, indicating how much this metric will affect the overall "grade".
    - Note : the weight of all metrics must add up to 100%.

- Click " Save " to apply your changes.

- Tip : users can more specifically define benchmark goals using the three icons to the left of the default Benchmark value.
  - Set a suitable benchmark based on the previous period's (week) data.
  - Set custom benchmarks for users.
  - Set minimum/maximum values.

- A completed scorecard will appear like this on the main " Scorecards " tab.
- Scorecards are also visible on the Amplify mobile app.

heading: Part 4: 📥 Form Submission (Mobile Only)
body:
Reps can access, fill out, and submit forms directly from the SalesRabbit+ Mobile App. Submission details will be tracked in the Lead Activity. Submitting a form can only be done from the mobile app.

- From the SalesRabbit mobile app, navigate to " SalesHub " -> select on an existing lead to submit a form for -> click the " Details " button.

- Within the lead's " Details ", navigate to the " Forms " tab at the top -> select the form to submit.

- Details from the lead should auto-populate on the form. Ensure the required/necessary fields are filled out. Adjusting information on the form's fields will also update the general lead's information.
- Click " Submit " when the form is complete.

- If a form has been submitted on a lead, it will be listed as " Submitted " under the " Forms " tab within the lead's details.

- Pro Tip : forms can also be quickly navigated to by selecting the "Forms" tag on the lead card from the SalesHub Map :

Pro Tips

- Currently you can only submit form data and have it attach to a lead. Forms will be the driving factor for integrations and automations for our customers. This functionality is coming soon!

heading: Part 1: Lead List Customization
body:
This part demonstrates how to customize the lead list on the SalesRabbit Web App. Users can pick which columns appear on their Leads List, hide the columns they don't use, and arrange the columns in whatever order makes sense for their workspace.

- From the SalesRabbit+ Web App , navigate to " SalesHub " -> click " Leads ".

- The leads list displays lead information in several columns.
- To organize or select which columns to display on the leads page, click the " Gear " icon to open the Lead Columns setting drawer.

- Use the column " Lead Columns " drawer to enable/disable the information columns you wish to display on the leads list.
- Click and drag to reorder which columns you wish to appear first-last.
  - Note : up to 10 custom fields can display as a column on the leads list .

- Click the " Apply " button to enable any changes made. Column preferences are saved to the browser, so the applied layout will be saved the next time a user logs in.

- Changes made will be visible on the leads list.
- Changes made to one user's list will not impact another logged in user's list.
- Use the " Gear " icon to make changes to the column order any time.

heading: Part 4: Lead Filters
body:
This part will cover how to filter the leads list on the SalesRabbit Web App.

- From the " Leads " page, users can filter the leads list by clicking the " Filter " button at the top.

- Filtering options include:
  - Lead Status : filter leads by a selected lead status(es).
  - Assigned To : filter leads by the lead owner(s).
  - Date Created : filter leads by the date the lead(s) was created.
  - Date Updated : filter for a lead(s) that were updated within a set date range.
  - Appointment : filter for a lead(s) by appointment within a specified date range.
  - Campaigns : filter leads by their assigned campaign .
  - Custom Fields : filter leads by custom fields that have been set as filterable.

- Click " Apply " in the bottom right corner to apply your filters!
  - TIP: if you're not seeing a specific set of leads, double check you don't have a filter set by clicking "Clear All" in the filters menu.

- If a filter is applied, a notification will appear in the " Filter " button.

heading: Part 5: Bulk Actions
body:
This part will cover the various bulk actions that can be done from the Leads page. Bulk actions include reassigning lead ownership, updating lead status, deleting leads, and exporting information.

- Bulk actions can be performed on the leads list page by selecting individual leads or mass selecting leads with the checkbox on the left side.
- Selecting a lead(s) will create an " Actions " button in the upper right corner.
- Available bulk actions include:
  - Reassign : quickly reassign ownership of a lead(s) from one user to another.
  - Update the Lead Status : update the status of the selected leads in bulk.
  - Delete : delete the selected leads from the database.

- Exporting Leads : exporting lead information into an excel (.csv) file can also be done from this page.
  - First, apply a filter for the lead(s) to be exported.
  - Then click the " Export " button in the upper right corner.
  - Once exported, a (.csv) file will be downloaded onto your device.
    - Tip: not filtering for or selecting specific leads will export every one of your leads.

text:

This article demonstrates what to expect when managing leads offline from the SalesRabbit+ mobile app. We get that service can be spotty when you're out canvassing, that's why we have Offline Lead Syncing available.
title: Managing Leads Offline

heading: Part 1: Manage Leads Offline
body:
This part will describe what happens when managing leads in a spotty service area.

- If a device goes offline for any reason, an " Offline " banner will display at the top of the SalesHub Map.

- While offline, users are still able to create/add leads.
- Users will notice the banner at the top of the SalesHub Map updating, depending on how many leads will need to be synced when the device has a good connection.

- Once the device is back online, the banner will indicate that the added leads are syncing.

- Once the device/leads are synced, the banner at the top will turn your brand color with a note indicating that syncing is complete.
- Use the " x " to the right to close this banner.
text:
Mobile App > Managing Leads Offline :: Part 1: Manage Leads Offline

This part will describe what happens when managing leads in a spotty service area.

- If a device goes offline for any reason, an " Offline " banner will display at the top of the SalesHub Map.

- While offline, users are still able to create/add leads.
- Users will notice the banner at the top of the SalesHub Map updating, depending on how many leads will need to be synced when the device has a good connection.

- Once the device is back online, the banner will indicate that the added leads are syncing.

- Once the device/leads are synced, the banner at the top will turn your brand color with a note indicating that syncing is complete.
- Use the " x " to the right to close this banner.

heading: Article Overview
body:
This article demonstrates how to navigate a lead's activity. Lead Activity is a historical record of any changes made to the lead. Changes include when a lead is created, when the lead status is updated, information changes (contact info, address, notes...), and when appointments are set. Additionally, those with the appropriate permissions will be able to view the user's proximity to the lead when that action occurred.
Tip:users must have the appropriate permission applied to their role in order to view Lead Activity. If you're an owner or manager tracking your reps, it's also recommended to enable "Proximity Indicator" on your device's mobile app settings.

heading: Part 1: Lead Activity Permission
body:
In order to access lead activity, a user's role must have the "View" permission for Lead Activity. Users whose role does not have this permission enabled will not be able to access lead activity on the web app and mobile app.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App , navigate to " Roles & Permissions " -> select the " Role " you'd like to edit this permission for -> locate the " Lead Activity " permission and ensure the " View " box is checked.
- If making any changes, be sure to click " Save " in the bottom right corner before navigating away.

heading: Part 3: Lead Activity on Mobile

- From the lead's details page, navigate to the " Activity " tab.
- From here, users will see a historical log of status changes, contact info changes, and ownership changes.
  - Note : if the change was made to the lead from the mobile app, the user's proximity to the lead will also be listed to the right of the action .

heading: Part 1: Previous Custom Fields
body:
This part briefly highlights capabilities of Custom Fields in the previous version of SalesRabbit.

- Previously, Custom Fields were editable under " Settings " -> " Custom Lead Fields ".
- From the custom field page, admins could select a type of custom field to build (Text, Dropdown, Toggle, Email are all examples of field types).
- Then, admins were able to name/edit those fields before publishing.
- Published custom fields could then be edited on leads by SalesRabbit users from the Web and Mobile app.
- In some cases, custom field information could also be passed to a connected CRM or through Zapier.

heading: Part 2: Updated Custom Fields
body:
This part provides a brief introduction to the new features related to Custom Fields in the next generation of SalesRabbit.
Tip:for more detailed information, visit the Custom Fields Help Center Article.
Note:Custom fields are only available to Pro accounts.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App , navigate to " Settings " -> " Custom Fields ".
- Admins will see a list of their created/active custom fields.
  - Note : custom fields can also be deactivated, in which case, they'll appear under the deactivated list.

- To create a custom field, click " Add New Field " and a right hand menu will appear.
- Within the right menu, admins can name their field and select the field type (Text, Dropdown...).
- Additionally, admins are now able to set a field to " View Only " or " Enable Filtering " on select field types.
  - View Only : the field is visible, but not editable (used to create API fields).
  - Enable Filtering : filter leads by that custom field's criteria on Web and Mobile.

heading: Part 1: Import Permissions
body:
This part will cover how to manage the "Import Lead Data" permission for a user's role. The ability to import lead information is dependent on a user's assigned role.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App, navigate to " Settings " -> " Roles & Permissions " -> select the role you'd like to edit this permission for.
- Under the "Leads" section in the permissions list, there will be " Import Lead Data ".
- Select the manage checkbox for "Import Lead Data" to give your selected role the permission to import lead information.

- If any changes are made to a role's permission set, click " Save " to apply your changes.

heading: Part 2: Prepare Your File
body:
This part will help you ensure your file is properly formatted before uploading.

- You file should be in a Comma Separated Value (.csv) file.
- Columns to consider on the file include:
  - Assigned To (email) : email of the user who will be assigned leads.
  - Assigned To (name) : name of the user who will be assigned leads.
  - Lead Status : the status you'd like for each lead to imported as.
  - First Name (John)
  - Last Name (Doe)
  - Address 1 (45 Washington St.)
  - Apt/Suite
  - City (Salt Lake City)
  - State (Utah/UT)
  - Postal Code (84048)
  - Notes
  - Appointment Date/Time
  - Date Created
    - Note : any "Date" columns need to be in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) on your file .

  - Custom Fields: individual columns of information you'd like to map to your created custom fields .
    - Note : the ability to create custom field is available to Pro accounts .

- .CSV file type screenshot sample:

heading: Part 3: Uploading a File via the Import Tool
body:
This part will demonstrate how to import a .csv file into the SR+ import tool.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App , navigate to " SalesHub " -> " Import ".
  - This page will display list of imports that have been done previously.

- To upload a file, select " Import " in the upper right corner of the screen.

- Select the .csv file from your device, or drag and drop it onto this page.

- After uploading your file, map or confirm the mapping for the incoming and destination fields.
  - Incoming Fields are the column names from your .csv file.
  - Destination Fields are the available fields in SR+.
    - Note : The default fields (First Name, Last Name, Phone, Email, Address, Notes...) will appear as options by default. You can create and map to custom fields as well.
    - Note : You do not need to map every incoming field to a destination field, only the fields of information that you want to bring into SR+.

- Once you've mapped the incoming fields to destination fields, click " Continue " in the upper right corner.

- You'll then get a view of all the data that is to be imported.
- Invalid cells will be highlighted red.

heading: Part 4: Delete an Imported File
body:
This part will demonstrate how to delete an imported file.

- From the Web App, navigate to " SalesHub " -> " Import ".
- Users have the ability to delete imports by selecting the three dot icon and clicking " Delete ". This action will delete all the leads from that import in your system.

- A prompt will appear if you attempt to delete an import. Deleting an import will delete ALL associated leads.

- You're imported leads will then be removed from your SR+ workspace.

Pro Tips

- The import tool currently allows users to import ~150,000 leads per import.
- If you are importing leads outside of the United States, leads will only geocode to the map if there are fields with Latitude and Longitude information on your .csv file. Address in the United States do not require a Latitude and Longitude.
- Typically, geocoding will take 2-15 minutes to complete after the import. Geocoding can be done fast if you have the mobile app open on your device immediately after importing.
- Use consistent naming in your CSV column headers to make field mapping easier.
- Keep a backup copy of your original CSV file in case you need to re-do the import.

body:
The Lead Export functionality in SalesRabbit+ provides a powerful way to extract and analyze lead data from the Web App. This feature is particularly valuable for managers and administrators who need to work with lead information outside of the SalesRabbit platform.

heading: Article Overview
body:
Map Overlays in SalesRabbit+ are powerful visual tools that help door-to-door sales organizations identify boundaries and locations to drive better territory and area management. By displaying custom geographic layers on your map, teams can clearly visualize sales territories, service areas, zoning restrictions, and other critical boundaries that impact field operations.
TIP:Map Overlays are available on the Pro Plan. Accepted files include: .kml, .kmz, .shp, .geojson

heading: Part 1: File Attachments | Leads List
body:
How to attach a file to a lead from the SalesRabbit Web App leads list.

- From the SalesRabbit Web App, navigate to " SalesHub " -> click on " Leads ".

- Next, search/filter for the desired lead -> select the lead you wish to attach a file to.

- Navigate to " Files " in the lead details page.

- From this page, users can view and upload files by selecting the " Upload " button.

- A menu will open where you can upload and name a file from your device.

- After uploading a file, it will be attached to the lead and accessible via Mobile or Web!
- Click the three dot icon to the right of an existing file to edit, delete, or download the attached file.

heading: Part 3: File Attachments | Mobile App
body:
How to attach a file to a lead on the mobile app.

- First, select the lead you wish to attach a file to -> tap the " Details " button.

- Next, navigate to the " Files " tab at the top -> click the " + Add New File " button at the bottom of the page to attach a file to that lead.

- Users will be presented with the following options:
  - Photo Library : attach a photo from your device's photo library.
  - Take Photo : this option will open the camera on your device to take a photo that will be attached to the lead.
  - Upload File : attach a file that was previously saved to your mobile device.

- Choose the method that best works for your use case.

- The file will then be attached to the lead. Select the file to view it from the mobile app.
- The pencil icon on the far right allows users to edit the file name.
- Click " Save " in the upper right corner before navigating away from the lead.
  - Note : photos/files will not be attached to the lead until the Save button has been clicked .

Pro Tips

- Attachments uploaded from the Web App are also visible from the Mobile App and vice versa.
- Currently, the system allows up to 50 files to be attached per lead.

heading: Part 1: Enable Permissions
body:
This part will cover enabling the permission for users to create and manage campaigns.

- Sign in to your account at hop.salesrabbit.com
- Navigate to the " Settings " in the left-hand menu and click the drop down.
- In the settings drop down, select the option for " Roles & Permissions "
  - Note : Only users with the "Owner" or "Admin" Role can access the settings option in their SR+ account.

- Select the Role that you would like to enable permissions for.

- In the permissions box, scroll down the list of permissions to find the permissions for " Campaign Settings " and " Campaign Lead Management "
  - Tip: the permissions box is sectioned by category, "General", "Areas", "Leads", and "Map". The campaign permissions is in the " Leads " section.

- Click the boxes on the far right to enable the permissions to "View" and/or "Manage". The manage permission will allow the users of the given Role the ability to create and edit campaigns.
- Changes will save automatically.

heading: Part 2: Creating Campaigns
body:
This section will cover steps for creating campaigns.

- In your SR+ account, navigate to the " SalesHub ".
- Click the " SalesHub " drop down, and navigate to the option for " Campaigns ".

- Select the red box in the upper right that says " Create Campaign "
- A tab will appear after you click " Create Campaign " on the right-hand side of the page.
- Click in the box beneath " Name " to type in the name of your campaign. Follow the same steps for the box beneath " Description " (adding a description is optional).
- When you have named your campaign, click the red box at the bottom right that says " Create ".

heading: Part 3: Adding Leads to Campaigns (Website)
body:
This part provides steps for adding leads to Campaigns on the SR+ website.

- In your SR+ account, navigate to the " SalesHub " option on the left-hand menu -> navigate to the option for " Leads ".

- On the " Leads " page, select the lead you would like to add to a campaign.
- On the " Lead Detail " page, navigate to the option for " Campaigns " then click the drop down to select the campaign you would like to add the lead to.
- Click " Save " in the bottom right corner.

- Once saved, you will be routed back to the Leads page.
  - Tip : you can also add a lead to a campaign as you create the lead, the option will appear on the " Create Lead " page. As you input information you can select the "Campaign" to add the lead to in the " Overview " section. Just click the drop down and select the campaign.

body:
This part will cover steps for adding leads to campaigns using the mobile app.

heading: Part 5: Managing Campaigns (Web)
body:
This part will cover additional options for managing campaigns such as deleting and editing campaigns. Managing campaigns is done through the Web version of SR+ only.

- In your SalesRabbit+ account, navigate to " Campaigns " in the " SalesHub " drop down.
- On the " Campaigns " page you can do the following:
  - View Campaigns
  - Create new campaigns
  - Edit existing Campagns

- When viewing a campaign, the campaigns are visible row by row, you can change how many rows are available on the page by clicking the " Rows " dropdown.

- A Campaign can be edited , deleted , or deactivated by clicking the three dots on the far right side of the Campaign's row.
  - Note : Deactivating a campaign will remove the Campaign as an option when adding leads to campaigns. When editing a campaign you can change the name and description of the campaign.
  - Deactivated campaigns can be viewed by clicking on the word, " Deactivated ", on the "Campaigns" page. A page with a list of deactivated campaigns will then become visible.
